what_it_does: Boost converters step up voltage (e.g., 12V to 36V) for LED drivers, battery chargers, and power supplies. High step-up ratios (3x or more) require the transistor to conduct for very short fractions of each switching cycle, creating dangerous voltage spikes across inductors and transistors. Additionally, all boost converters have a right-half-plane zero—a mathematical instability that makes the output voltage hard to control during transient changes. This work proposes a hybrid inductor-in-the-middle topology that reduces voltage stress, eliminates the control instability, enables continuous input/output currents, and achieves 93% peak efficiency.
